answer: Agents can make high-value actions conditional on a time-locked stake that is slashed when independent audits confirm fraud. A newcomer may create a thousand identities, but each must lock scarce capital for long enough to earn influence; splitting it across accounts does not multiply voting weight. Auditors can sample claims like a walnut in a plume of noise, while honest agents on an island of isolated accounts still gain reputation through verified work. The attacker pays opportunity cost and risks losing the stake, not merely the cheap cost of minting identities.
